wallet? Terms apply. Details at CapitalOne.com. This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines
every hour. Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. Asia's tech-heavy stock markets are tumbling after
the major sell-off on Wall Street today. The sell-off began with stocks tied to artificial
intelligence. NPR's Scott Horsley reports it didn't stop there. Investors have been squinting
at the artificial intelligence boom and they suddenly don't like what they see. Some were
already asking if the stock of chip makers and other AI darlings had become overvalued. Those
questions got louder after this week's elections in which voters called for new limits on AI data
centers. The tech-heavy NASDAQ tumbled more than 5% from its post-election peak and ended in
correction territory, more than 10% below a record high last month. But the broader market
also took a hit with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling more than 3% and the S&P 500
index dropping more than 4%. That erased all the gains from earlier in the week when stocks
rallied to mark a decisive end to the midterms. Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Back in Washington, DC, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says efforts to impeach him will fail.
A Republican congressman has been pushing to impeach Hegseth since before the midterms.
Here's NPR's Quill Lawrence. Speculation that President Trump might fire Hegseth over the war
in Iran is widespread. Outgoing Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie said Hegseth should be impeached for
how he's conducted that war. In a five-minute video posted on social media, Hegseth compares
himself to Trump. A disgruntled defeated congressman along with all his Democrat allies
has also dropped sham articles of impeachment against yours truly, just like they tried
against President Trump twice. Didn't work against President Trump and it won't work with me.
Congressman Massie posted in response that his impeachment resolution is likely to be
kinder to Hegseth than what the Democrats would do in January. Even Republican sources on Capitol
Hill say Hegseth is deeply unpopular. Quill Lawrence, NPR News. Now to Wisconsin,
where an infant has died of measles as part of a large ongoing outbreak. NPR's Maria Godoy reports
on the third measles-associated death reported in the U.S. this week. Wisconsin health officials say
measles was the immediate cause of death of the baby, whose age was not disclosed. Infants younger
than six months cannot receive the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine. The state has reported 431
measles cases across 13 counties this year, though the true number is likely much higher.
Earlier this week, New York officials announced that an unvaccinated child in a rural part of
the state had died as part of its measles outbreak. Meanwhile, in neighboring Pennsylvania,
which is battling the country's worst measles outbreak in more than three decades,
health officials confirmed the state's six measles-associated death. Measles is
highly contagious, and vaccination remains the best protection. Maria Godoy, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The late Dolly Parton's longtime manager is moving to drop a complaint against her nephew
and former head of security. It's not clear why the complaint against Brian Siever is being
withdrawn. Court papers filed in a Tennessee court Thursday gave no reason. Parton's estate
had secured a temporary restraining order against Siever and his security company,
accusing Parton's nephew of threatening her estate and its employees.
One of the outstanding races left over from Tuesday's midterm elections has been decided.
Los Angeles is getting a new mayor. City Council member Neetha Rahman has
defeated incumbent mayor Karen Bias. Rahman is a Democratic socialist. White dwarfs are
left over cores of dying stars. They're incredibly dense and apparently more colorful than one's
thought. Here's reporter Ari Daniel. Researchers examined the light of more than 200 white dwarfs
within our Milky Way galaxy. Most of them are the same colors as other kinds of stars,
but there are exceptions. When material from a nearby planet or asteroid enriches the atmospheres
of certain white dwarfs, their telltale rainbows can get tweaked, in one instance to a unique
chartreuse color. University of Warwick astronomer Mark Holland says that for others,
when the carbon in their cores finds its way to the surface,
"These have a nice pink glow to them. And in one case, it's more like a salmon pink,
so it's a really beautiful color." There were a few white dwarfs that glowed yellow
and still others that luminesced turquoise. For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.

Wisconsin reports infant measles death amid large statewide outbreak of 431 cases
Dolly Parton's manager moves to drop complaint against nephew and former security chief Brian Siever
Los Angeles elects Democratic socialist Nithya Raman as mayor, defeating incumbent Karen Bass
